fit: clinical review of Parkinson dementia and psychosis
assessment: Discusses formed events and illusions and reviews medication studies. It supplies no dietary comparison or episode treatment effect of its own.
Fly electrophysiology measures stimulus-evoked response and contrast. It cannot measure spontaneous or subjective clinical events.

fit: resting functional connectivity in fluctuating Lewy body dementia
assessment: The sixteen-person Lewy body comparison assessed cognitive fluctuations and connectivity. Associated visual symptoms do not provide a food exposure or clinical episode rate.

fit: persistent thought disorder item in genotyped Parkinson comparison
assessment: Sustained hallucinations by a composite thought-disorder threshold differed between genetic subgroups. Time to the threshold is distinct from a count of visual events.

fit: autoimmune encephalitis and GABA-A receptor antibodies
assessment: A separate clinical syndrome includes a visual event amid seizures and delirium. It supplies no transfer to dried figs or usual Parkinson visual episodes.

fit: five botanical exposures and negative geotaxis in Parkinson-model flies
assessment: The source distinguishes opposing Bacopa climbing outcomes across genotypes, and reduced control climbing with Centella. Its preparation list and endpoint do not match.

fit: EEG prediction and clinical feature presence in an MCI cohort
assessment: Visual hallucination status appears in the clinical table, while EEG and diagnostic conversion are the measured prognostic assessments. No culinary contrast is present.

fit: commentary on an evoked visual hallucination case
assessment: The commentary repeats the primary stimulation case and compares possible networks. It supplies no independent clinical exposure or diet result.

fit: electrically elicited visual scenes in a person evaluated for epilepsy surgery
assessment: Different stimulation sites elicited formed visual scenes or distorted face perception. These provoked responses do not measure spontaneous clinical Parkinson episode frequency.

fit: sleep-attack review with co-occurring hallucination terms
assessment: The source table separates visual and auditory experiences in cited dopamine agonist cases. Its primary outcome is sudden sleep onset, and case modality is secondary reporting.

fit: primary dopamine agonist sleep attack case series
assessment: The primary abstract confirms a nine-person sleep case series. The visual case detail comes from the later table, and original case body access remains open.

fit: regulatory tables and maintenance adverse-event narrative
assessment: Open conversion and randomized maintenance have distinct denominators and coding. The 2015 label includes a composite; the full approval package has an explicitly visual maintenance withdrawal.

fit: reanalysis of the earlier ceremonial pharmacokinetic cohort
assessment: Fourteen of 15 earlier volunteer profiles underlie the reanalysis. Time profiles for another mixed botanical exposure do not establish a clinical Parkinson event frequency.
